_about: Checker-schema translations of the enumerator's checkable candidates (open-problems/candidates.json), written by the lean thread. Each row keeps the original English commitment beside the formal one and a one-sentence reading. uses_illustrative_values and origin are carried through unchanged: an elimination of a proposed-here candidate with illustrative values eliminates the enumerator's own numbers, not a published hypothesis. Reason codes and the policy against inventing numbers: lean/eliminate/translations.json _about.

candidates.problem: Origin of sexual reproduction. What were the fundamental selective forces responsible for the origin of sexual reproduction?

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: proposed-here (written by the enumerator, not literature)
candidates.original_statement: Sex originated in isogamous unicells without separate males: every sexual individual is itself a fecund parent, so at equal per-individual fecundity the asexual:sexual per-generation growth ratio was 1, not 2.
candidates.checkable_rationale: The twofold-cost constraint states the growth ratio is 2 when sexual lineages spend half their offspring on males at equal fecundity; it decides whether that premise is absent here (ratio 1) or present (ratio 2).
candidates.reading: The candidate sets the growth ratio to 1 by denying the model's premise (isogamy, no males); the twofold-cost theorem is conditional on anisogamy with males contributing nothing, so it cannot rule on a model without males.

cannotRule.C5: premise-rejected: the candidate posits isogamy with no males; the theorem assumes a 1:1 sex ratio with males contributing nothing

candidates.problem: Origin of sexual reproduction. What were the fundamental selective forces responsible for the origin of sexual reproduction?

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: proposed-here (written by the enumerator, not literature)
candidates.original_statement: Sex originated in an anisogamous population (half of offspring male) and was favoured from the first generation because each sexual offspring had relative fitness (1+s) with s >= 1 over an asexual offspring.

original_commits.quantity: required per-offspring advantage of sexual offspring

candidates.checkable_rationale: With equal fecundity the asexual lineage grows twice as fast; the candidate survives only if (1+s) >= 2.
candidates.reading: The candidate concedes anisogamy but adds a per-offspring fitness advantage (1+s >= 2) for sexual offspring; the model has equal fitness and no selection term, so the theorem cannot say whether the advantage compensates.

cannotRule.C5: outside-model: a fitness advantage of sexual offspring is not in the model (equal fecundity and viability); the theorem fixes only the twofold term the advantage must offset

candidates.problem: Maintenance of sexual reproduction. What are the fundamental selective forces maintaining sexual reproduction?

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: published hypothesis, quantitative condition added by the enumerator
candidates.original_statement: Red Queen: parasites track common asexual clones, so common clones become disproportionately infected and are replaced by initially rare clones, periodically favouring genetically diverse sexuals (source). Quantitative form added here: sexuals persist if the time-averaged (geometric-mean) relative fitness of asexuals, after parasite-induced reduction, is <= 1/2 of its parasite-free value.

original_commits.quantity: required geometric-mean parasite-induced fitness reduction of asexuals (added here)

original_source.name: abstract returned by `orx discover`
original_source.paper_title: The Maintenance of Sex, Clonal Dynamics, and Host-Parasite Coevolution in a Mixed Population of Sexual and Asexual Snails

candidates.checkable_rationale: The factor 1/2 is exactly the offset needed against the twofold growth advantage at equal fecundity.
candidates.reading: Parasite-induced fitness reduction of asexuals is a term the model lacks; the candidate's factor 1/2 is chosen to offset the twofold term, which the theorem fixes but cannot weigh against a reduction it does not model.

cannotRule.C5: outside-model: parasite-induced fitness reduction is not in the model; the theorem fixes only the twofold term it must offset

candidates.problem: Maintenance of sexual reproduction. What are the fundamental selective forces maintaining sexual reproduction?

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: published hypothesis, quantitative condition added by the enumerator
candidates.original_statement: Lineage selection: within populations asexuals win (short-term twofold disadvantage of sex conceded), but asexual lineages have higher extinction rates, so sex is maintained at the level of lineages (source). Quantitative form added here: with asexual lineages arising at rate tau per sexual lineage and going extinct at rate e_a, sexual lineages persist at a non-zero share only if e_a exceeds e_s + tau.

original_source.name: abstract returned by `orx discover`
original_source.paper_title: Lineage Selection and the Maintenance of Sex

candidates.checkable_rationale: The constraint fixes the within-population term the lineage-level argument must overcome; it cannot rule on the extinction-rate inequality itself.
candidates.reading: The conceded within-population advantage 2 is read as the per-generation factor on the odds of asexual females, which is the theorem's own quantity; the lineage extinction-rate inequality is outside every constraint.
notFormalised: lineage extinction rates e_a, e_s and origination rate tau: no constraint

candidates.problem: Maintenance of sexual reproduction. What are the fundamental selective forces maintaining sexual reproduction?

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: proposed-here (written by the enumerator, not literature)
candidates.original_statement: Asexual females arising in sexual populations have at most half the fecundity of sexual females (developmental costs of parthenogenesis), so the twofold advantage never materialises.

original_commits.quantity: fecundity of asexual relative to sexual females

candidates.checkable_rationale: The constraint's premise is equal fecundity; it decides that the twofold advantage holds unless fecundity differs, which is exactly what this candidate claims (so it checks the premise, not the conclusion).
candidates.reading: The candidate denies equal fecundity (asexual fecundity at most 0.5 of sexual), which is the model's premise; the theorem does not say what happens under unequal fecundity.

cannotRule.C5: premise-rejected: the candidate posits unequal fecundity; the theorem assumes equal fecundity

candidates.problem: Determinants of cell size. How do cells determine what size to grow to before dividing?

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: proposed-here (written by the enumerator, not literature)
candidates.original_statement: Division is triggered by surface-to-volume limitation: a spherical cell growing isometrically has transport capacity ~ r^2 and demand ~ r^3, so it divides when r reaches r* = 3*J/q (J: area-specific uptake flux, q: volume-specific demand).
candidates.checkable_rationale: Isometric growth with area ~ L^2 vs volume ~ L^3 is exactly the square-cube premise.
candidates.reading: 'Demand ~ r^3' is volume (weight at constant density) with exponent 3 (C7b); 'transport capacity ~ r^2' is an area with exponent 2 (C2a, now formalised as R2); both are the hypotheses restated, so consistent; the formula r* = 3J/q is a design rule no theorem covers.
notFormalised: critical radius r* = 3J/q: a design rule beyond the scaling laws

candidates.problem: How do organs grow to the correct shape and size? How are the final shape and size of organs so reliably formed? These processes are in part controlled by the Hippo signaling pathway.

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: proposed-here (written by the enumerator, not literature)
candidates.original_statement: Growth stops when self-weight stress reaches tissue strength sigma*: for an organ growing isometrically, weight ~ L^3 over supporting section ~ L^2 gives stress ~ L, so L_final = sigma* / (c * rho * g) for a shape constant c.
candidates.checkable_rationale: Square-cube scaling gives the stress ~ L dependence the candidate relies on.
candidates.reading: 'Weight ~ L^3' (C7b), 'supporting section ~ L^2' (C2a) and 'stress ~ L' (C8e, R7 with R1) are the theorems' own exponents under isometry; consistent. L_final = σ*/(c ρ g) is the size limit cannot_carry gives in form, with constants no theorem supplies.
notFormalised: L_final = σ*/(c ρ g): the constants c, ρ, g, σ* are not supplied by any theorem

candidates.problem: Why are all leaves the size they are, and not an order of magnitude larger or smaller? How is the upper limit on leaf size set?

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: proposed-here (written by the enumerator, not literature)
candidates.original_statement: A leaf scaled isometrically by k: blade area ~ k^2, blade mass ~ k^3 (thickness scales too), petiole cross-section ~ k^2; petiole bending stress ~ (mass x lever arm)/section modulus ~ k^4/k^3 = k; the upper limit is where this stress reaches petiole strength.
candidates.checkable_rationale: Isometric mass vs cross-section scaling.
candidates.reading: 'Blade mass ~ k^3 (thickness scales too)' is the body-like load of R9a (C7b, exponent 3); 'petiole cross-section ~ k^2' is C2a; 'petiole bending stress ~ (mass x lever arm)/section modulus ~ k^4/k^3 = k' is exactly R9a conclusion 1 (C12, exponent 1), so the candidate is consistent, not eliminated; 'the upper limit is where this stress reaches petiole strength' is the existence of L_max,b (bending_cannot_carry), whose value needs sigma_max and the shape constants. The candidate chose the R9a fork by committing to thickness scaling; under R9b (constant thickness) no limit would follow.

cannotRule.C8e: not the quantity of the lemma: C8e is axial stress W/A; the stress of this candidate is bending stress, ruled on by C12

notFormalised: the value of the petiole size limit (sigma_max and the shape constants are not supplied); wind loading (dynamic) is outside R9

candidates.problem: Cambrian explosion. What is the cause of the apparent rapid diversification of multicellular animal life around the beginning of the Cambrian, resulting in the emergence of almost all modern animal phyla?

problem_source.name: Wikipedia, 'List of unsolved problems in biology'

candidates.provenance: proposed-here (written by the enumerator, not literature)
candidates.original_statement: All crown animal phyla diverged within a window of T_w = 20 Myr; under neutrality the pairwise per-site divergence accumulated within the window is 2 mu T_w (0.04 for mu = 1e-9 per site per year), so inter-phylum molecular distances must be dominated by the time since the window.
candidates.checkable_rationale: Neutral rate = mu and budget mu*T per lineage directly fix the expected divergence.
candidates.reading: 'Under neutrality the divergence within the window is 2 mu T_w' commits each lineage's substitution rate to equal mu = 1e-9 per site per year (the identity k = mu is unit-free, so per-year values are checked as given); the window T_w = 20 Myr is not checked by any constraint (no M, no site count).

candidates.checkable_rationale: As above.
candidates.reading: As WP-055/C1: the excess divergence 2 mu x 100 Myr commits k = mu = 1e-9 per site per year; the 100 Myr lead time is not checked by any constraint.
